The legs of an isosceles right triangle are increasing. The length, measured in feet, of each leg is given by $x(t)=t+{t}^{2},$ where $t>0$ is the time in seconds. What is the rate of the change of the length of the hypotenuse after $2$ seconds? Give your answer rounded to $1$ decimal place.
question.worked_solution:
In the diagram,

- $x$ is the length of the equal sides, and

- $z$ is the length of the hypotenuse.

As shown in the diagram, $x,$ $x,$ and $z$ form a right triangle with $z$ as the hypotenuse. We wish to find the rate of change of $z,$ which is $\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}.$

First, we determine the length of the equal sides after $2$ seconds. We get 

$$
x=x(2)=(2)+(2)^{2}=6\text{ ft}.
$$

We can find $z$ using the Pythagorean Theorem, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{x}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ {6}^{2}+{6}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ 72 & ={z}^{2} \\ z & ≈8.485\,3\,\text{ft}\end{aligned}
$$

The rate of change of the sides is given by $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}={x}^{′}(t)=2t+1.$ So, when $t=2$ their velocity is

- $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}={x}^{′}(2)=2(2)+1=5\text{ ft/s}.$

Finally, we differentiate both sides of ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}={z}^{2}$ with respect to $t$ and then substitute the known values, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({z}^{2}) \\ 2x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} \\ 2(6)(5)+2(6)(5) & ≈2(8.485\,3)\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} & ≈7.1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the hypotenuse's length is changing at a rate of $7.1\text{ ft/s}$ after $2$ seconds.
